big_picture: The Iran war is turning into a blockade and a shadow war: Rubio says major combat is no longer needed, while Iran lifts its missile-range limit and threats reach US officials and bases in Britain. Oil steadied (Brent about $92.5). The Houthis claim new strikes on Riyadh airport and Aramco. The Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi are called productive, but a ceasefire is not on the table, and Ukrainian drones hit the Ust-Luga oil port. Nvidia fell another 5.5% to $168.89 as the Huang affair reaches the cabinet; it reports on Nov 17. In Washington the Hegseth impeachment was shelved 211–204. Signal's Carnival and Lufthansa put ideas reached their entry ranges (CCL $30.74, LHA €8.69); a ceasefire would hurt both.

stories.title: US–Iran: Rubio says no more major combat needed, while Iran's threats move west
stories.reality: Washington is shifting from bombs to money: Rubio says "major combat operations" are no longer needed because the economic offensive and the naval blockade are doing the damage. Iran is not standing down: it lifted its self-imposed 2,000 km missile-range limit, the US moved more aircraft out of UK bases over an Iranian threat, Treasury Secretary Bessent was moved to a military base after alleged threats on his life, and US prosecutors charged three alleged Iranian operatives over plots including the RAF Fairford air base. France blames Iran for hacking supermarket fridges and weighs sanctions; Iran denies it. No answer from Tehran on Qatar's ceasefire proposal has been reported.
agreed: Rubio, after the G7 in Paris: no need for major combat operations; economic pressure and the blockade are working (NYT, Breitbart, France 24).
The IRGC announced it lifted the 2,000 km limit on its ballistic missiles (RT, Al Jazeera).
The US moved military aircraft from a second British base over an Iranian threat (NBC, Fox News).
Bessent was moved from his home near Washington to a military base after alleged Iranian threats (NYT, CNBC, Jerusalem Post).
The US charged three alleged Iran-backed operatives over plots in Europe and the US, including RAF Fairford (BBC, DW, Al Jazeera).

stories.reality: The Houthis keep up their campaign against Saudi Arabia: on Nov 10 they claimed four missile and drone operations on Riyadh airport and Aramco facilities. A key Saudi oil pipeline was hit again, this time with the Houthis denying it. Syria is weighing sending troops to help Saudi Arabia. There is still no Saudi confirmation of lost oil output.

stories.title: Ukraine: the Abu Dhabi talks are "productive", but no ceasefire on the table
stories.reality: The first Russia–Ukraine talks since February ran about four hours on Nov 10 under US mediation (Kushner, Witkoff) and resumed on Nov 11. The US calls them "very productive" and "constructive" and wants a "new" European security framework; prisoner exchanges are on the agenda. A ceasefire is not. The war goes on around the talks: Ukrainian drones set fire to the Ust-Luga Baltic oil-export port, and Russia says it downed about 150 drones near St Petersburg.

Rubio called them "very productive"; Kushner "constructive" (TASS).

stories.title: Nvidia: the Huang affair reaches the cabinet; the AI trade wobbles as Anthropic eyes a record IPO
stories.reality: Nvidia fell another 5.5% on Nov 10 to $168.89 (−25% in a month). The affair now reaches the administration: Trump says the FBI is investigating, the NYT says he was reminded of the intelligence before his China trip, and a report says Commerce Secretary Lutnick got a memo on it. Nvidia hired Wachtell Lipton (former prosecutor Joon Kim) for an independent probe; Huang apologized. Megaspeed, the alleged spy's company, is under US investigation for smuggling Nvidia chips into China. Around it the AI trade is mixed: SoftBank posted a $7 billion loss and revised its US data-centre plans (GE Vernova fell), while Anthropic set an IPO range of $70–78 a share (about $1.4 trillion), with bankers reportedly preparing to raise it. Nvidia reports on Nov 17.

Nvidia hired Wachtell Lipton to lead an independent investigation (BBC, MarketWatch).

stories.title: Washington: Hegseth impeachment shelved 211–204; Jordan and Thune lead a shrunken GOP
stories.reality: The House voted 211–204 to refer Massie's impeachment resolution against Hegseth to committee, killing it until Democrats take over in January; 11 Democrats, including Pelosi, missed the vote. Hegseth called it a "farce"; Trump praised the outcome. Republicans picked Jim Jordan and John Thune as their leaders for the next Congress, while some Democratic senators oppose Schumer. The Senate advanced the bipartisan permitting bill.

stories.title: Israel: new Knesset sworn in; Eisenkot breaks off talks with Likud
stories.reality: The new Knesset was sworn in with an opposition majority. Eisenkot, who has the first chance to form a government, pledged an official October 7 inquiry and to reverse many of Netanyahu's policies, then cancelled coalition talks with Likud after Netanyahu's speech claiming Arab parties seek Israel's destruction. He still has no coalition.

market_calls.why: Oil fell 8% in a month on peace-talk hopes, but a US–Iran deal looks unlikely (15%), more US strikes are likely (60%) and the Houthis keep hitting Saudi targets. The risk premium is more likely to come back than to fade.
War risk in the Gulf, falling US yields (10-year down 8% in a month) and a possible US shutdown all support gold.

Three-way Ukraine talks with Europe at the table this week (85%) keep "peace" headlines coming. A real ceasefire is unlikely (12%), so the drop should be modest, and much is already priced in (Rheinmetall is −57% from its high).
Airlines rallied hard (+20% in a month) as oil fell. If oil's risk premium returns, they are the first to give it back.

Down 26% in a month: a lot of bad news is priced in. The Trump–Xi meeting (85% it happens) can bring a relief rally on export rules. This is a short-term bounce call, not a call that the selloff is over.
About 120x earnings, falling even after beating expectations, and AI-bubble worries hit the whole sector. Momentum is down (−19% in a month), but strong growth limits the downside.

Trump is winding the Iran war down, Qatar has a ceasefire proposal on the table, and Congress is turning against the war (the Hegseth impeachment vote). ITA rose 3.9% on the last day, so part of the risk premium can fade. Barely better than a coin flip: defence budgets don't change with one ceasefire.
